note: Known high/critical advisories in production dependencies, each named with the ticket
that owns the fix. The gate (scripts/check-audit.mjs) fails on any high/critical
advisory NOT listed here, so this file is the line between 'debt we have already
booked' and 'something new'.
Adding an entry is an explicit, reviewable decision — give the id, the package, and
the ticket or reason. Removing entries is the point: the weekly audit workflow fails
when a listed advisory is no longer reported, so a fix prunes its own line.
The list was 27 entries — booked on 2026-08-06/07 against #101 and #104 — and #101
cleared all of them: an in-range `pnpm update` (the lockfile was sitting at the floor
of ranges that already allowed the patched versions), one devDependency pin raised so
tailwindcss would stop deduping onto a vulnerable postcss, and #104's swiper 12 major
before it. It then sat empty until 2026-10-03.
Two of those entries needed no fix of their own. The `image-size` pair had no published
patch and were expected to sit here for a while; payload 3.87.1 dropped the dependency,
so they left the graph instead of being waited out. Worth remembering the next time an
unpatched transitive looks permanent.
A refilled list re-arms the gate's 'the audit stopped looking' tell — zero findings
against a non-empty baseline. check-audit.mjs also sizes the graph it walked, which is
what covered that gap while the list was empty. Read the comment there before assuming
a green run means anything.
